processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: As-cast ingot (50 Kg) prepared by vacuum induction melting under high purity Ar atmosphere was homogenized at 1150 °C for 4 h. Shared precursor for the whole alloy.
Subsequently hot-rolled (HR) into rods with a diameter of 16.5 mm.
Solution-treated at 1050 °C for 2 h followed by oil quenching to obtain equiaxed grain structures; this is the parent process (proc_st-1050c-2h-oq) of the LNT impact sample.

processing_steps.method: instrumented Charpy V-notch impact test at liquid nitrogen temperature
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Charpy V-notch impact test on standard specimens (55 mm in length, 10 mm in width, 10 mm in thickness, V-notch depth of 2 mm) recording force-displacement and energy-displacement curves at LNT.

structures.overall_structure: After LNT impact deformation, the austenite remains highly stable with no phase transformation; the impact deformation substructure is characterized by dislocation cells or cell blocks, similar to the tensile substructure, together with deformation twins and a small amount of microbands. Low temperature promotes the formation of deformation twins, but they do not burst as in TWIP steels.

microstructure_list.region: near the fracture surface (crack propagation zone), EBSD sampling area

phases_present.morphology: small fraction distributed in the austenite matrix

defects.type: fine cracks around voids generated by detachment of α phase at γ/α interface

grain_structure.texture: strongly banded/elongated colour contrast along the impact direction, suggesting twinning and slip bands (IPF map along impact direction)

microstructure_list.region: approximately 1000 µm from the fracture surface

defects.type: dimples of micrometer/sub-micrometer size with some larger deep voids (ductile fracture)

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Fine cracks are present around the voids generated by the detachment of the α phase in the cryogenic impact sample; the γ/α interface serves as the crack initiation site for the cryogenic impact sample, which may contribute to the decrease in crack propagation energy at low temperature.

interfaces.slip_behavior: Impact deformation substructure consists of dislocation cells or cell blocks, with deformation twinning activated more readily at LNT.
interfaces.phase_evolution: No phase transformation occurs in the austenite under LNT impact; both phases are highly stable.
interfaces.interface_notes: The existence of ~3.0 % α phase in the austenite matrix reduces impact energy by about 30 % from RT (331 J) to LNT (254 J).

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: standard Charpy V-notch specimen: 55 mm in length, 10 mm in width, 10 mm in thickness, V-notch depth of 2 mm
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: instrumented Charpy V-notch impact test recording force-displacement and energy-displacement curves

comparative_performance.improvement_percentage: -30 % (impact energy reduced from 331 J at RT to 254 J at LNT)

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: standard Charpy V-notch specimens, tested at LNT; force-displacement and energy-displacement curves recorded
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure impact toughness and separate crack initiation/propagation energy of the LNT impact specimen
characterization_methods.key_findings: Impact energy 254 ± 6 J at LNT; crack initiation energy (Wm) 99.19 J and crack propagation energy (Wp) 156.71 J at LNT.

characterization_methods.technique: EBSD phase mapping and IPF mapping in SEM
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: near the fracture surface in the crack propagation zone, 20 µm scale bar maps
characterization_methods.purpose: Check phase stability and impact deformation substructure/orientation near the LNT fracture surface
characterization_methods.key_findings: Phase map almost entirely γ with a small α fraction (no phase transformation); fine cracks around voids at γ/α interfaces; IPF along impact direction shows strongly banded/elongated colour contrast suggesting twinning and slip bands.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: transmission electron microscope operated at 200 kV (FEI-Tecnai G2 F20)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: region approximately 1000 µm from the fracture surface; 500 nm scale bars; SAED insets
characterization_methods.purpose: Reveal the impact deformation substructure near the LNT fracture
characterization_methods.key_findings: Dislocation cells or cell blocks plus deformation twins (markedly promoted at low temperature) and possible microbands.

characterization_methods.purpose: Determine the fracture mode of the LNT impact specimen
characterization_methods.key_findings: Fracture surface composed mainly of dimples of micrometer/sub-micrometer size with some larger deep voids, indicating ductile fracture at LNT.

unmapped_findings: For the LNT impact sample the instrumented Charpy test gave a crack initiation energy Wm = 99.19 J and a crack propagation energy Wp = 156.71 J (Fig. 2c); the text states crack initiation is ~80–100 J at both RT and LNT while crack propagation changes from 251 J at RT to 156 J at LNT, meaning the LNT Charpy impact is governed by crack propagation energy.

Macroscopic fracture appearance of the LNT impact sample shows only a small number of subordinate cracks and small necking (in contrast to the large necking and many subordinate cracks at RT), which contributes to the lower crack propagation energy at LNT.

The impact energy of the LNT impact specimen is reduced about 30 % from 331 J at RT to 254 J at LNT, attributed to the existence of ~3.0 % α-phase in the austenite matrix (the γ/α interface acting as crack initiation site).
Deformation twins are more readily activated under LNT impact but do not burst as in TWIP steels, so twins make a non-significant contribution to the impact energy of the LNT impact sample.
The LNT impact fracture is ductile (dimpled) for both micrometer and sub-micrometer dimples, and the austenite shows no phase transformation despite the LNT impact deformation.
